name: Qwen3.8-27B-Q8_0
architecture_basis: [DOC] architecture read from unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF - the GGUF repository keeps the base model's config.json beside the files, and its figures are identical to Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B's own
[DOC] layer_types names 16 full_attention layer(s) that allocate a cache, of 64 layers, the last 0 sharing an earlier layer's; [DOC] head_dim=256 and num_key_value_heads=4

[DOC] layer_types names 48 linear-attention layer(s); one holds a convolution state of 61,440 bytes ([DOC] this repository's copy of the configuration states torch_dtype='bfloat16', the older spelling of the key the base model's own config.json writes as dtype) and a temporal state of 3,145,728 bytes ([DOC] mamba_ssm_dtype='float32')

[DOC] the two state figures are what the pinned vLLM allocates: v0.25.1 vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_5.py:524-542 sizes a linear-attention layer with MambaStateShapeCalculator.gated_delta_net_state_shape, and vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/mamba_utils.py:213-233 makes its conv state (linear_key_head_dim x linear_num_key_heads x 2 + linear_value_head_dim x linear_num_value_heads) = 10,240 wide by (linear_conv_kernel_dim - 1) = 3 at 2 bytes, and its temporal state linear_num_value_heads x linear_value_head_dim x linear_key_head_dim = 786,432 elements at 4 bytes. Both files read from the v0.25.1 tag.
[OBS] these factors multiply out to 65,536 bytes per token, which is the figure this row stores - 2 x 16 layers x 4 heads x 256 head_dim x 2 bytes.

[UNKNOWN] at file level. These figures are the BASE MODEL's architecture, not a reading of the GGUF itself. [OBS] Hugging Face's model API exposes only architecture, context_length, total and totalFileSize for this repository, not key_length or head_count_kv, so the file itself cannot be checked from here. What would settle it: gguf_dump on the actual file, or the llama-server startup log it produces.
notes: [OBS] the llama.cpp path. The named file is 29,047,086,048 bytes, read from Hugging Face's own tree listing; weight_bits is that size against the 27,320,697,856 parameters the repository's GGUF metadata states, which is 8.51 bits each.

[OBS] the repository publishes 28 other quantisations of the same weights, from UD-IQ1_S at 6.19 GB to UD-Q8_K_XL at 31.46 GB, and a two-part BF16 set. This row names one of them. Adding another is a new row naming another file, never an edit to this one.

[DOC] the architecture both pinned runtimes need is present in both. vLLM v0.25.1 registers Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration at vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py:560, and llama.cpp b10143 (commit 88b47a755c72fed4b22fba0fd262e2d7b7d01583) declares LLM_ARCH_QWEN35 as "qwen35" at src/llama-arch.cpp:41 - which is the architecture string this repository's own GGUF metadata carries. Neither has been observed loading this model on real hardware.
[DOC] context_length 262,144 is what this repository's own GGUF metadata states, and it agrees with max_position_embeddings in the config.json beside it.

[DOC] this family is image-text-to-text: Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B's own config.json carries a vision_config beside its text_config, and that repository publishes preprocessor_config.json and video_preprocessor_config.json. Every architecture figure on this row is the TEXT model's. [UNKNOWN] what the vision tower costs on a card at serving time; nothing here sizes it.

[OBS] the repository also publishes mmproj-BF16.gguf and mmproj-F16.gguf, which is what llama.cpp would need to see an image. This program downloads the ONE file this row names, so a backend started from it serves text.
[DOC] the repository is public - its model record answers gated=false, so a download needs no licence acceptance.
[DOC] generation_config.json not published at unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF; read from base Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B's own generation_config.json (temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 20), fetched 2026-09-06.

name: Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B
architecture_basis: [DOC] architecture read from ornith-ai/Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B's own config.json, fetched 2026-09-10: architectures Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration, model_type qwen3_5_moe - an image-text-to-text row; the figures below are its text_config, the same shape as nex-agi/Nex-N2.5-mini's.

[DOC] text_config.layer_types names 10 full_attention layer(s) that allocate a cache, of 40 layers (every 4th, full_attention_interval=4), the last 0 sharing an earlier layer's; [DOC] head_dim=256 and num_key_value_heads=2

[DOC] text_config.layer_types names 30 linear-attention layer(s); linear_key_head_dim=128, linear_num_key_heads=16, linear_value_head_dim=128, linear_num_value_heads=32, linear_conv_kernel_dim=4, mamba_ssm_dtype='float32', dtype='bfloat16', identical to Ornith-1.0-35B's text_config: one layer holds a convolution state of 49,152 bytes and a temporal state of 2,097,152 bytes, (128x16x2 + 128x32) x 3 x 2 + 32x128x128x4 = 49,152 + 2,097,152 = 2,146,304
[OBS] these factors multiply out to 20,480 bytes per token, the same figure Ornith-1.0-35B stores for the identical text_config shape.
[OBS] https://huggingface.co/api/models/ornith-ai/Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B?blobs=true, fetched 2026-09-10: 16 safetensors shards summing to 71,903,871,064 bytes.
[DOC] reasoning_parser and tool_call_parser copied from the Ornith-1.0-35B model (both Qwen3-family models, the same reasoning and tool-call templates apply).
notes: [DOC] https://huggingface.co/ornith-ai/Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B/raw/main/generation_config.json, fetched 2026-09-10: temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 20; no min_p or repetition_penalty key.
